cells: 2430 / Erdős 995 — modern lacunary L2 partial-sum question: must sum_{j<=N} f(n_j x)=o(N sqrt(log log N)) hold almost everywhere for every f in L2 and every lacunary integer sequence? https://www.erdosproblems.com/995 ; historical context: Erdős, Compositio Math.16 (1964),52–65, printed57–58.

Boon Suan Ho, Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks, arXiv:2604.18535v2 (21 April 2026), Theorem1.6 and Section7. Existing full negative answer to the modern Erdős995 question: for every fixed finite real p>=2, there are a real mean-zero f in Lp(T) and one deterministic sparse dyadic sequence n_j=2^{m_j}, n_{j+1}/n_j>=2, such that on one full-measure set the limsup of sum_{j<=N}f(n_j x)/[N(log N)^{1/p-epsilon}] is +infinity simultaneously for every epsilon>0. The function and sequence may depend on p, but not on x or the later choice of epsilon. The case p=2 refutes the proposed o(N sqrt(log log N)) bound. The exact modern formula is not literally printed on Erdős's1964pp57–58: those pages display a lower log-log scale and an upper log scale. DOI identifies the arXiv family; the verified proof is v2, PDF SHA256 f88b36a072d66476c5948061b7f2fc4d61dc536bbc5df5aa5bd3cdd2a84a82d0. This row credits an existing preprint, not a new project theorem/upload or a formal peer-review claim. Source acknowledges GPT-5.4 Pro assistance; PR1275 is an AI-assisted audit. Fourier-tail/EP996 results, logarithmic endpoints, optimal secondary factors, and consecutive-dyadic/bounded-gap variants are outside this acceptance.
